requirements.requirement: Provision the local accounts designer, reviewer, and visitor.
requirements.summary: All three accounts were created and remained present after reboot. Final evidence also shows locked credentials and private, account-owned home directories.

requirements.requirement: Ensure new directories and documents created by designer inherit reviewer read/write access while remaining owned by designer.
requirements.summary: Tests using designer with umask 077 created both files and nested directories with inherited reviewer permissions. Reviewer successfully read, traversed, wrote, and appended, while ownership remained designer:designer. The complete behavior was repeated successfully after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Prevent visitor from accessing the project content.
requirements.summary: The ACL explicitly denies visitor, and direct identity tests denied directory listing, file reading, and writing for newly created content before and after reboot. Access to the preserved existing file was also denied.

requirements.requirement: Provide inherited access without a periodic permission-repair job.
requirements.summary: Access and default POSIX ACLs are present on the project directory, nested objects demonstrably inherited them, and inheritance continued after reboot. Bounded checks of standard cron and systemd configuration found no project-targeting repair job.

The prepared project contained brief.txt with SHA-256 5c077cd26fc7d84d4c43e9b5dfa674428ab1ce50c38422e63678d35043f43082. Its hash, size, ownership, and presence remained unchanged in final and post-reboot observations, with verification artifacts removed.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL remained at 10.0 and the kernel remained 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 before and after execution and reboot. The ACL tooling and matching libacl revision came from the enabled RHEL 10 BaseOS repository, had valid Red Hat signatures, installed successfully, and passed package verification.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledged the restart, returned with a different boot ID independently confirmed by lifecycle observations, and demonstrated recovered services, accounts, ACLs, protected data, and identity-based access behavior.
limitations: The periodic-fixer search was bounded to standard cron locations, /var/spool/cron, and /etc/systemd/system using the exact project path; an indirect or unusually located job would not be detected. Direct default-ACL behavior before and after reboot nevertheless establishes that the delivered access mechanism itself is inherited and persistent.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. The initial DNF attempt downloaded the packages later used by the successful cache-only installation; importing the verified Red Hat keys enabled signature-checked installation. Account creation, ACL changes, package installation, bounded access-test artifacts, and the restart all directly supported task completion or mandatory evidence collection. Test objects and the incidental GPG inspection directory were removed, the transient reboot unit disappeared with reboot, package health remained good, no failed services or new listeners appeared, and final temporary-file differences were normal per-boot systemd directories.
